Use Tier 2: replace the residual MultVAE expert’s full-history reconstruction objective with masked-item denoising, focusing on data_processing_and_feature_engineering, model_design, and training_evaluation. The latest fusion-only trial reached macro validation HR@10 of 0.6062, below the reported best of 0.6250, so the next experiment should improve the learned representation rather than tune fusion weights. The residual encoder-to-decoder path can encourage reconstruction of visible items, whereas recommendation requires ranking an unseen next item; this is a plausible limitation to test.

For each training history containing at least two distinct items, randomly hide 20% of its items, retaining at least one visible item and one target. Encode only the remaining items and compute multinomial reconstruction loss exclusively on the hidden training items, retaining the existing KL term and annealing schedule. Keep singleton histories on the existing reconstruction objective so every training user remains represented. Preserve the VAE architecture, SASRec expert, optimizer settings, and current global fusion weight, making masked-item denoising the single experimental change.

Train one revised VAE per category with seed 42, using only the supplied training splits and respecting the shared runtime budget. Select checkpoints using the fixed validation HR@10 protocol and compare the four-category macro average against the unchanged ensemble. At inference, supply the complete available history without artificial masking, and ensure validation and the generated working/predict.py use identical model loading, history processing, and fusion logic; held-out predictions remain the host evaluator’s responsibility.
